title: Enterprise Networking, Security & Automation (CCNA 3)
subtitle: Connect, secure, manage and automate a multi-site enterprise network
audience_line: Participants who completed CCNA 2 and are preparing the CCNA exam
overview: This programme is the third of three courses that prepare the Cisco CCNA 200-301 exam, aligned with Cisco Networking Academy Enterprise Networking, Security and Automation v7. Participants route between sites with single-area OSPFv2, filter traffic with access control lists, connect to the internet with NAT and PAT, and study WAN technologies, VPNs with IPsec, and QoS. They manage, design and troubleshoot the network, and automate it with REST APIs and Python. A timed practice exam covers the three courses, and the programme closes with a final project: a documented enterprise branch network.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Participants who completed CCNA 2 and are preparing the CCNA exam

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Switching, Routing & Wireless Essentials (CCNA 2), or equivalent: VLANs, inter-VLAN and static routing. These topics are not taught again; no prior Python needed

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 42 h: 36 h of chapters + 6 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs on simulated Cisco devices; one timed practice exam

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: Runs locally: one laptop per participant with Cisco Packet Tracer (free with a Cisco Networking Academy account; its network controller serves the REST API labs) and Python 3; physical Cisco routers for selected labs when the organiser provides a rack; no cloud account or cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase, a timed practice exam and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete the labs and the project

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can build, secure and manage a multi-site network with OSPF, ACLs and NAT, read device data through a REST API with Python, and sit the CCNA 200-301 exam

phases.name: OSPF
phases.focus: Single-area OSPFv2 configuration, tuning and troubleshooting
phases.intro: Participants replace static routes with a dynamic routing protocol: single-area OSPFv2, its neighbours and link-state database, then DR and BDR election, cost tuning and default route propagation. Validated lab: three sites routed by OSPF, with a default route to the internet learned by every router.

chapters.title: OSPF in Practice
chapters.content: Multi-access networks, DR and BDR, cost, default route propagation, troubleshooting

phases.name: Security, ACLs & NAT
phases.focus: Threats, access control lists, NAT and PAT
phases.intro: Participants review the threats an enterprise network faces, then filter traffic with standard, extended and named ACLs placed where they belong, and connect private addressing to the internet with static NAT, dynamic NAT and PAT. Validated lab: a security policy written as ACLs, tested against allowed and denied flows, with users reaching the internet through PAT.

chapters.title: Network Security Concepts
chapters.content: Threats, attack types, security best practices

chapters.title: ACL Configuration
chapters.content: Standard, extended and named IPv4 ACLs, securing VTY access

phases.name: WAN, VPN & Network Management
phases.focus: WAN and SD-WAN, VPNs and IPsec, QoS, management protocols
phases.intro: Participants compare WAN technologies, see how site-to-site and remote-access VPNs protect traffic with IPsec and GRE, how QoS gives priority to sensitive traffic, then manage devices with CDP, LLDP, NTP, SNMP and syslog and back up configurations and IOS images. Validated lab: routers synchronised by NTP, sending syslog and SNMP data to a management server, with configurations backed up.

chapters.title: WAN Concepts
chapters.content: WAN topologies and technologies, broadband, SD-WAN overview

chapters.title: VPN & IPsec Concepts
chapters.content: Site-to-site and remote-access VPNs, IPsec, GRE

chapters.title: QoS Concepts
chapters.content: Traffic characteristics, queuing, QoS models and mechanisms

chapters.title: Network Management
chapters.content: CDP and LLDP, NTP, SNMP, syslog, configuration backup and IOS image management

phases.name: Design, Automation & CCNA Review
phases.focus: Scalable design, troubleshooting, SDN, automation, practice exam
phases.intro: Participants design hierarchical networks that scale and troubleshoot them with a method, see how virtualization, SDN and controllers such as Catalyst Center change network operations, and read device data through a REST API with a short Python script. A timed practice exam across the three CCNA courses closes the phase. Validated lab: a Python script that lists the devices known to the Packet Tracer network controller.

chapters.title: Network Design & Troubleshooting
chapters.content: Hierarchical and scalable design, troubleshooting methodology and tools

chapters.title: Network Virtualization
chapters.content: Cloud, virtualization, SDN and controller-based networking

chapters.title: Network Automation
chapters.content: REST APIs, JSON and YAML, configuration management tools, Catalyst Center, AI in network operations

chapters.title: CCNA 200-301 Review
chapters.content: Timed practice exam across the three courses and debrief

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: An enterprise branch network, documented and tested
phases.intro: Each participant builds the network that connects a branch to its head office from a written brief, reusing the phase labs, then documents and tests it before presenting it to the group.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: Read the brief, then configure OSPF between sites, the ACL security policy and PAT to the internet

chapters.title: Manage, Automate & Document
chapters.content: SNMP, syslog and NTP; a Python script that reads device data through a REST API; site-to-site VPN design; test plan and documentation

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Test results and live demo; questions and feedback

project.title: Enterprise Branch Network
project.brief: A branch connected to its head office: OSPF between sites, an ACL security policy, PAT to the internet, a site-to-site VPN design, SNMP, syslog and NTP management, and a Python script that reads device data through a REST API; documented and tested.
project.stack: Cisco Packet Tracer and its network controller, Cisco IOS routers and switches, OSPFv2, ACLs, NAT, SNMP, syslog, NTP, REST API, Python
project.deliverable: Packet Tracer file, Python script, design document, test results, live demo
